A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Meta-rater study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and substantial appendix reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model pre-training experiments, downstream evaluations, rating-model results, and ablations, including additional results in Appendix H.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds benchmark evaluations, metric-correlation analysis, and a proxy-architecture sensitivity experiment.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, LightGBM weight prediction, top-ranked data selection, weight averaging, and the PRRC rating procedure remain unchanged. The 46M proxy is an added sensitivity-test configuration, rather than a replacement for the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds MMLU and NaturalQuestions as challenging, knowledge-intensive evaluations across three model sizes. SlimPajama and the original eight downstream tasks remain. Experiments with 7.2B models already existed in v1.

E2.justification: Corresponding main, scaling, and combination-strategy comparisons retain their comparator sets. The added MMLU/NaturalQuestions evaluation uses existing comparators: Random and, for 1.3B models, QuRating-Educational Value. No new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: v3 adds an 18M-versus-46M proxy comparison, increasing hidden size from 256 to 512 and layers from two to four. It also specifies 200k SlimPajama examples for the correlation analysis. Existing training and few-shot settings remain unchanged; benchmark-specific demonstration counts for MMLU/NaturalQuestions are not supplied.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic analysis with correlations among 25 raters, a PCA visualization of the loss landscape, and sensitivity to proxy architecture (Sections 4.2.1 and 5; Figures 4–5). Existing proxy-count, combination-strategy, and domain analyses remain. The learned-weight discussion is moved from v1 Appendix B.1, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: v3 adds Spearman correlation estimation across 25 quality metrics using 200k examples; the earlier Kendall-tau annotation-model comparison remains. This adds statistical association reporting, but neither version supplies repeated-run variability, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 and corresponding retained appendix scores are unchanged. v3 adds correlation results, 94.6% overlap between selections from different proxy architectures, MMLU/NaturalQuestions scores, and per-task 7.2B results. It removes the 50B-token scaling rows. New findings are mixed: Table 19 reports 7.2B NaturalQuestions scores of 10.42 for Meta-rater versus 10.89 for Random.

T1.justification: The task formulation, aggregation equations, and FLOPs approximations remain unchanged. The new correlation and PCA analyses provide empirical diagnostics, without introducing mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The central multidimensional-selection, doubled-convergence-speed, and 3.23-point improvement claims remain. v3 foregrounds scalability to 7.2B in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, using evidence already present in v1. Its abstract also expands the release claim from annotated data to scripts, data, and models.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning complementary quality metrics, proxy-size stability, and local minima explaining the advantage of learned weights. Appendix I adds discussion of near-chance MMLU performance and capacity limitations. However, Section 4.2.2's favorable interpretation of the new benchmarks overlooks counterexamples in Table 19. The original Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a project repository link and states that scripts, data, and models are released, extending v1's annotated-data announcement. It also identifies the 18M architecture explicitly as the proxy and documents the added 46M configuration. Existing prompts, annotation splits, hardware, hyperparameters, and training times are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bai et al. (2024) on collaborative data selection and the MMLU and NaturalQuestions references. Its positioning relative to RegMix and existing quality-selection approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 fixes duplicated weight-generation prose and several language errors, splits Section 4.2 into metric analysis and model results, moves the weight discussion into the main text, and shortens the conclusion. The overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds a correlation heatmap, a loss-landscape plot, and a benchmark table; merges the main scaling tables; and restructures the appendix scaling table. It also systematically narrows and reflows the four prompt panels and 24 example panels, and resizes or relocates appendix tables. Existing performance and distribution plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the study more assessable through the proxy-architecture check, correlation analysis, fuller 7.2B results, and explicit resource-access information. These address gaps in v1's diagnostic evidence and reproducibility documentation. The gains are limited by removal of the 50B-token results and overstated interpretation of the new benchmarks: Table 19 includes worse 7.2B NaturalQuestions performance than Random despite Section 4.2.2's broadly favorable claim. The primary method and main results remain unchanged.
